newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul stock exchange launches Eurobond market.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul stock exchange launches Eurobond market.

text.p: The Istanbul stock exchange launched an international bond market on Monday to facilitate trading of Turkish Eurobonds.
"At the moment, there are few buyers and sellers. I expect it to develop slowly," a private banker said of the newly-opened market.
"We expect activity to increase in March," said a foreign banker.
The market is open from 0800 to 1500 GMT. The exchange's Eurobond trade screen showed four bids and one ask, with no deals made so far at 1115 GMT.
Turkey's 40 international issues, launched since late 1988, are listed on the market, including 11 Samurai, nine Euromark and 13 Eurodollar bonds.
Bankers, who welcomed the market, said they expected initial trade to be in dollars and marks.

"This is a good market, and banks in Turkey will be increasingly interested," said an Istanbul banker. "These papers are usually held in investment portfolios. With this market, I think there will be more activity."

The new market, a free trade zone, aims to boost trade in Turkish Eurobonds, which were hindered by high taxes and a haphazard over-the-counter trade in London. Daily trading was about $2-million in London.
Turkish stock exchage officials expect trading to reach $50 million a day by the end of the first year.
